title: Lipschitz continuity of the Gaussian mean derivative
statement: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$, and let $v>0$. The function $c\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{z-c}{v}p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz$, where $p_v(c,z)$ is the Gaussian density with mean $c$ and variance $v$, is Lipschitz with constant $2/v$.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is a nonzero nonnegative real, hence positive
replaced: Let $v>0$ and $p_v(c,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-c)^2/(2v))$. For measurable $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with $|f|\le1$, the function $c\mapsto\int((z-c)/v)p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz$ is globally $2/v$-Lipschitz.
